items.title: Ukraine and Poland form drone working groups in technology exchange deal

items.title: Diehl Defence opens new 155mm artillery shell body line in Germany
items.summary: Diehl Defence officially opened a new 7,000 square metre production line in Röthenbach, Germany, for DiNa 155mm artillery shell bodies following an investment in the mid double-digit millions of euros. sections.label: What happened
lines: Diehl Defence officially opened a new 7,000 square metre production line in Röthenbach, Germany, for DiNa 155mm artillery shell bodies following an investment in the mid double-digit millions of euros. The project builds on the ARGE DiNa joint venture established by Diehl Defence and Nammo in 2019, with Diehl Metal Forgings manufacturing the shell bodies and Nammo providing design and technology expertise.

sections.label: Context
lines: 2019: Diehl Defence and Nammo established the ARGE DiNa joint venture to serve the German market with DiNa 155mm artillery rounds.
Jun 2024: The project to convert a production hall at Röthenbach for DiNa shell body manufacturing began.
Oct 2026: Pilot production started on the new 7,000 square metre production line following an investment in the mid double-digit millions of euros.
10 Nov 2026: Diehl Defence officially opened the new production line for DiNa 155mm artillery shell bodies in Röthenbach, Germany.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: EU — White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030 and ReArm Europe Plan (2025-03-19): Close critical capability gaps in seven priority areas (including air and missile defence and artillery) and build a stronger European defence industrial base; ReArm Europe enables over €800 billion of defence spending.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following the establishment of the ARGE DiNa joint venture in January 2019 and the launch of the conversion project in June 2024, pilot production began in October 2026 and culminated in the opening of the new line in November 2026, aligning with EU objectives to close critical artillery gaps and strengthen the European defence industrial base.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: DiNa 155mm artillery shell bodies depends on forging presses and forming equipment — Shell bodies manufactured by Diehl Metal Forgings.
DiNa 155mm artillery shell bodies depends on DiNa round design, technology, and manufacturing expertise — supplied by Nammo.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Procurement and supply chain professionals in European defence should monitor this expansion as a benchmark for scaling domestic artillery manufacturing capacity through cross-border industrial partnerships.

items.title: BlackSky Secures Seven-Figure MoD Assured Contract for Gen-3 Tasking
items.summary: BlackSky Technology secured a seven-figure Assured subscription contract with an unidentified international ministry of defence for priority Gen-3 tasking and Spectra AI analytics.

sections.label: What happened
lines: BlackSky Technology secured a seven-figure Assured subscription contract with an unidentified international ministry of defence for priority Gen-3 tasking and Spectra AI analytics.

sections.label: Context
lines: 7 Sep 2021: BlackSky went public via a merger with Osprey Technology Acquisition Corp., trading on the NYSE under the ticker BKSY.
19 Feb 2025: Rocket Lab successfully launched the first BlackSky Gen-3 Earth imaging satellite on an Electron rocket from Mahia, New Zealand.
4 Nov 2025: BlackSky announced more than $30 million in multi-year contract wins for its constellation capabilities (Contract).
25 Nov 2025: BlackSky launched and rapidly commissioned its third Gen-3 satellite to expand constellation capacity (Delivered).
12 Aug 2026: BlackSky secured a multi-year international defense contract expansion integrating Gen-2 and Gen-3 satellite intelligence (Contract).
14 Sep 2026: BlackSky announced its fifth Gen-3 satellite achieved "first light" imagery within 20 hours of launch, expanding tactical revisit capacity.

10 Nov 2026: BlackSky announced a seven-figure "Assured" subscription contract with a new unidentified international ministry of defense for priority Gen-3 tasking and Spectra AI analytics (Contract).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following multi-year contract expansions in August 2026 and fifth Gen-3 satellite deployment in September 2026, BlackSky's recent November 2026 MoD subscription highlights accelerating global adoption of rapid tactical ISR capabilities.

items.title: Congress Weighs Defense Budget Cuts as $1.5 Trillion Plan Fades
items.summary: As the December 11 funding deadline approaches, consensus grows that the White House's $1.5 trillion defense plan is dead, prompting analysts to game out alternative budgets ranging from $1 trillion to $1.25 trillion.

sections.label: What happened
lines: As the December 11 funding deadline approaches, consensus grows that the White House's $1.5 trillion defense plan is dead, prompting analysts to game out alternative budgets ranging from $1 trillion to $1.25 trillion.

sections.label: Context
lines: 23 Jan 2026: Publication of the 2026 National Defense Strategy setting defense priorities.
6 Nov 2026: AEI publishes "FY 2027 Defense Budget End Game" detailing cuts across $1 trillion, $1.1 trillion, and $1.25 trillion toplines.
10 Nov 2026: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stresses the critical nature of the lame-duck period for department funding as consensus grows that the $1.5 trillion plan is dead.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — 2026 National Defense Strategy (2026-01-23): Four lines of effort: defend the homeland (including Golden Dome missile defence), deter China in the Indo-Pacific, more burden-sharing by allies, and supercharge the US defence industrial base.

US — PAC-3 MSE framework agreement under the Acquisition Transformation Strategy (2026-01-06): Seven-year framework agreements for proven munitions, giving industry long-term demand so it invests in capacity; PAC-3 MSE output to rise from about 600 to about 2,000 a year, subject to Congress.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: While the 2026 National Defense Strategy initially prioritized major modernization and industrial base expansion, subsequent budget end-game analyses and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's warnings in late 2026 highlight imminent fiscal constraints and forced capability tradeoffs.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: ITAR and EAR: export licensing on defense articles and dual-use microelectronics components across prime munitions and aircraft supply chains (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense contractors and supply chain partners should prepare for potential reductions or delays in major aircraft and missile programs and adjust long-term production planning accordingly.

items.title: House Republicans Delay Hegseth Impeachment Vote
items.summary: House Republicans voted 211 to 204 to send Rep Thomas Massie’s proposed impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee. The procedural move effectively delays any potential floor vote on the matter until January.

sections.label: What happened
lines: House Republicans voted 211 to 204 to send Rep Thomas Massie’s proposed impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee. The procedural move effectively delays any potential floor vote on the matter until January.

sections.label: Context
lines: Feb 2026: U.S. forces initiate military operations against Iran without explicit congressional authorization, later designated by critics as Operation Epic Fury.
Oct 2026: A survey by the advocacy group Common Defense reveals active-duty and family dissatisfaction with the perceived politicization of the armed forces under current leadership.

10 Nov 2026: House Republicans successfully maneuver to send Rep. Thomas Massie’s impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, delaying any potential floor vote until the new congressional term.

lines: Following military actions against Iran in February 2026 and growing service member dissatisfaction revealed in October 2026, legislative maneuvers in November 2026 have postponed leadership accountability battles, signaling ongoing friction between executive military strategy and congressional oversight.

items.title: US Army targets 2029 for palletized M-SHORAD Increment 4 deployment
items.summary: The U.S. Army intends to reach the First Unit Equipped milestone for M-SHORAD Increment 4 in the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2030, targeting deployment by the end of 2029.

sections.label: What happened
lines: The U.S. Army intends to reach the First Unit Equipped milestone for M-SHORAD Increment 4 in the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2030, targeting deployment by the end of 2029.

sections.label: Context
lines: Sep 2020: General Dynamics Land Systems is awarded a contract modification for M-SHORAD Increment 1 prototyping and integration on Stryker vehicles (Contract).
May 2021: The U.S. Army begins fielding M-SHORAD Increment 1 (Sgt. Stout) utilizing Stryker platforms and Moog RIwP turrets.
8 May 2024: The U.S. Army issues a Request for Information (RFI) for M-SHORAD Increment 4 to protect light and dismounted maneuver forces.
27 Jul 2025: U.S. and U.K. forces evaluate counter-drone technologies under Project Flytrap to feed light air-defense requirements.
26 Mar 2026: The U.S. Army refines its M-SHORAD Increment 4 specifications around a Self-Loading Equipment Dock (SLED) or vehicle-agnostic pallet format.
8 Oct 2026: The U.S. Army schedules an Industry Day for M-SHORAD Increment 4 in Huntsville, Alabama, for late October.
27 Oct 2026: General Dynamics Land Systems and MSI Defense Solutions demonstrate a proposed M-SHORAD Increment 4 system on a Ford Ranger at AUSA 2026 (Plan).

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: NATO — The Hague Summit Declaration (2025-06-25): Allies commit to 5% of GDP a year by 2035: at least 3.5% on core defence requirements and up to 1.5% on broader security spending, including the defence industrial base.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: The M-SHORAD program is evolving from Stryker-based Increment 1 systems toward vehicle-agnostic, palletized Increment 4 solutions designed for light tactical vehicles and uncrewed platforms The program includes modular mounting decks, compact radar sensors, and integration with light tactical vehicles.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: Palletized Frame / Self-Loading Equipment Dock (SLED) depends on MSI Defense Solutions — modular mounting deck provider.
Radar Sensors depends on Echodyne — compact radar architectures for short-range detection.
Host Light Tactical Vehicles depends on GM Defense — Infantry Squad Vehicle / Infantry Utility Vehicle.

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: The program involves modular mounting decks provided by MSI Defense Solutions, compact radar sensors from Echodyne, and light tactical vehicles from GM Defense.

items.title: Hensoldt Targets €10B Sales by 2035 and Doubles Radar Output
items.summary: Hensoldt announced at its Capital Markets Day an ambition to reach €10 billion in annual sales by 2035 while doubling production capacity for the TRML-4D air defense radar over the next two years.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Hensoldt announced at its Capital Markets Day an ambition to reach €10 billion in annual sales by 2035 while doubling production capacity for the TRML-4D air defense radar over the next two years.

sections.label: Context
lines: 11 Jun 2018: Hensoldt unveils the TRML-4D C-band GaN AESA multi-function air surveillance and target acquisition radar for ground-based air defense at the Eurosatory exhibition in Paris, securing an initial order for 10 systems.
3 Feb 2025: Diehl Defence places a €100 million order with Hensoldt for TRML-4D radars, maintenance, and training packages (Contract).
25 Jul 2025: Hensoldt secures a €340 million contract package to supply additional TRML-4D and SPEXER 2000 3D MkIII radars to Ukraine (Contract).

19 Aug 2025: Hensoldt confirms a German Armed Forces order for six TRML-4D systems under the IRIS-T SLM program as part of the European Sky Shield Initiative (ESSI), scaling annual output targets to 30 units.

items.title: Pentagon Lacks Visibility Over F-35 Spares
items.summary: The GAO confirmed that the Pentagon still lacks visibility over millions of F-35 spare parts and fails to locate previously missing stock.

sections.label: What happened
lines: The GAO confirmed that the Pentagon still lacks visibility over millions of F-35 spare parts and fails to locate previously missing stock.

sections.label: Context
lines: 12 Apr 2019: Initial GAO audits highlight mounting transparency and logistics gaps in the F-35 sustainment supply chain.
15 Mar 2022: GAO reports that the Enterprise Logistics Management System (ELMS) fails to interface with prime contractor property systems.
24 May 2023: GAO reveals that a prime contractor lost over 1 million F-35 spare parts worth $85 million between 2018 and 2022 (USD 85 million).
Dec 2025: Quarterly Contractor Data Requirements List (CDRL) data shows extensive anomalies, including 6% of records priced at $0.01 or less.
31 Mar 2026: Joint spares pool reaches approximately 26 million parts valued at $31 billion, with 17,000 parts worth up to $2.5 billion missing from official property tracking (USD 31 billion).
15 Jul 2026: U.S. Air Force awards Lockheed Martin a $1.6 billion contract for additional spare parts (Contract, USD 1.6 billion).
9 Nov 2026: GAO releases report GAO-27-108713 confirming the Pentagon still lacks visibility over millions of parts and has failed to locate the pre-2023 missing stock.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Since initial 2019 audits highlighted transparency gaps, recurring issues like unlinked contractor property systems in 2022 and millions of missing parts in 2026 demonstrate persistent inventory tracking failures Signal: systemic lack of real-time asset accountability.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: F-35 Global Joint Spares Pool depends on tires, valves, fasteners, structural panels — Comprehensive inventory of 26 million components shared across U.S. services and international operators.
ITAR / EAR: export licensing on F-35 components global transit and repair loop (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense contractors and supply chain managers must improve inventory interface systems and data quality to address persistent DoD asset tracking deficits.

items.title: GAO: Over 1M F-35 Parts Still Missing

lines: A GAO report released on Nov. 9, 2026, revealed that more than 1 million F-35 spare parts remain missing and 26 million parts across 700 facilities lack real-time oversight.

sections.label: Context
lines: 30 Sep 2019: Pentagon financial audits reveal chronic systemic inability to track government property and inventory within major weapon systems like the F-35.

Oct 2020: JPO initiates targeted physical inventories across contractor- and government-managed facilities, spending upwards of $17,000,000 USD through fiscal 2025 without achieving accurate tracking (USD 17 million).

23 Jul 2026: Pentagon awards major F-35 spare parts acquisition contracts to support global fleet requirements (Contract).
9 Nov 2026: GAO releases report GAO-27-108713 stating that more than 1 million F-35 spare parts remain missing and 26 million parts across 700 facilities lack real-time oversight (USD 31 billion).

lines: Since 2019 financial audits have highlighted a chronic inability to track F-35 inventory, leading to unquantifiable material misstatements by September 2025 and ongoing tracking failures through late 2026.

items.title: Royal Navy Commissions 1st Autonomous Squadron
items.summary: The Royal Navy formally commissioned the 1st Autonomous Squadron at HMNB Portsmouth on 5 November 2026, replacing Project Beehive as a permanent front-line entity. The new squadron will operate uncrewed surface vessels including Kraken K3 Scout and Rattler boats around the clock.

sections.label: What happened
lines: The Royal Navy formally commissioned the 1st Autonomous Squadron at HMNB Portsmouth on 5 November 2026, replacing Project Beehive as a permanent front-line entity. The new squadron will operate uncrewed surface vessels including Kraken K3 Scout and Rattler boats around the clock.

sections.label: Context
lines: 5 Nov 2025: The UK Ministry of Defence published preliminary market engagement notices for a new uncrewed surface fleet under what would become Project Beehive (Plan).
10 Mar 2026: Contract award notice published showing Kraken Technology Group won the competitive procurement to supply 20 high-speed uncrewed boats (Contract, GBP 12.3 million).

11 Mar 2026: The Royal Navy officially confirmed the procurement of 20 uncrewed boats from Kraken Works (Kraken Technology Group) under Project Beehive to serve as testbeds for the Hybrid Navy (GBP 12.3 million).
20 Apr 2026: Rheinmetall and Kraken Technology Group established the joint venture Rheinmetall Kraken GmbH and commenced series production of the K3 Scout USV at the Blohm+Voss shipyard in Hamburg.

23 Jun 2026: BMT announced a contract award to support the Royal Navy's transition to a hybrid fleet by providing operational concept development, synthetic simulation, and risk analysis for Project Beehive (Contract).

10 Jul 2026: Kraken Technology Group and Capewell successfully completed world-first extracted-load airdrop trials of a Project Beehive K3 Scout USV from an A400M military transport aircraft using UMCADS parachute systems (Testing).
5 Nov 2026: The Royal Navy formally commissioned the 1st Autonomous Squadron at HMNB Portsmouth, replacing Project Beehive as a permanent front-line entity (Delivered, GBP 1.5 billion).

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following preliminary market notices in November 2025 and subsequent contract awards for K3 Scout testbeds in early 2026, the Royal Navy has transitioned its uncrewed vessel roadmap into a permanent operational squadron backed by four-year funding, signalling an accelerated shift toward a hybrid fleet.

items.title: US Ambassador details NATO 3.0 factory reset
items.summary: US Ambassador to NATO Matthew G. Whitaker detailed the NATO 3.0 concept, which emphasizes European defense and a strict focus on collective deterrence rather than out-of-area operations The policy requires all allies to increase defense spending to 5% of GDP and translate those commitments into concrete military capabilities.

sections.label: What happened
lines: US Ambassador to NATO Matthew G. Whitaker detailed the NATO 3.0 concept, which emphasizes European defense and a strict focus on collective deterrence rather than out-of-area operations The policy requires all allies to increase defense spending to 5% of GDP and translate those commitments into concrete military capabilities.

sections.label: Context
lines: 25 Jun 2025: NATO convenes The Hague Summit, where allies commit to scaling defence spending towards 5% of GDP.
12 Oct 2026: Commissioner Andrius Kubilius defines NATO 3.0 at the Warsaw Security Forum, outlining European conventional leadership.
8 Nov 2026: Lockheed Martin announces plans to invest over $8 billion to expand missile manufacturing capacity across eight sites (Plan).
9 Nov 2026: US Ambassador Matthew G. Whitaker details the NATO 3.0 factory reset, demanding focus on European defense and 5% GDP targets.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — 2026 National Defense Strategy (2026-01-23): Four lines of effort: defend the homeland (including Golden Dome missile defence), deter China in the Indo-Pacific, more burden-sharing by allies, and supercharge the US defence industrial base.

US — PAC-3 MSE framework agreement under the Acquisition Transformation Strategy (2026-01-06): Seven-year framework agreements for proven munitions, giving industry long-term demand so it invests in capacity; PAC-3 MSE output to rise from about 600 to about 2,000 a year, subject to Congress.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Following commitments at The Hague Summit to scale defense spending towards 5% of GDP, and Commissioner Andrius Kubilius outlining European conventional leadership, US Ambassador Matthew G. Whitaker detailed the NATO 3.0 factory reset demanding focus on European defense and 5% GDP targets, signaling a permanent shift toward localized European deterrence.

lines: Defense industry business development and procurement teams must align supply chains with long-term European rearmament and increased capacity demands.

EU — Council Regulation establishing the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument (2025-05-27): Up to €150 billion in EU loans for member states investing in defence industrial production through common procurement of priority capabilities.

lines: Following decades of regional alignment since their 2004 EU and NATO accession, the V4 nations are accelerating defense industrial synergies under Slovakia's 2026 presidency, supported by EU funding frameworks.

items.title: Neros Secures $450M Pentagon Loan to Scale Domestic Drone Production
items.summary: Neros Technologies secured a $450 million conditional loan commitment from the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital on November 2, 2026, matched by $165 million in company equity.

sections.label: What happened
lines: Neros Technologies secured a $450 million conditional loan commitment from the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital on November 2, 2026, matched by $165 million in company equity.

sections.label: Context
lines: 2023: Neros Technologies established in Torrance, California, focusing on low-cost, expendable uncrewed systems.
11 Oct 2025: Neros closes $75 million Series B funding round led by Sequoia Capital to expand manufacturing infrastructure (Funding, USD 75 million).

30 Jun 2026: U.S. Army awards Neros a firm-fixed-price IDIQ contract worth up to $500 million for Archer first-person-view (FPV) small unmanned aircraft systems under the Purpose-Built Attritable System (PBAS) programme (Contract, USD 500 million).
13 Aug 2026: Neros announces $250 million Series C funding round co-led by Sequoia Capital and American Strategic Technology Fund at a $2.5 billion valuation (Funding, USD 250 million).
30 Sep 2026: Neros secures a $100 million order for 14,000 drones and explosive payloads following its performance in Drone Dominance Program Gauntlet II (USD 100 million).

2 Nov 2026: The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) announces a $450 million conditional loan commitment to Neros to scale domestic component manufacturing, matched by $165 million in Neros equity (USD 450 million).

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — Unleashing U.S. Military Drone Dominance (Secretary of Defense memorandum) (2025-07-10): Ramp up US production and fielding of low-cost drones: buy American-made drones and parts, equip combat units, and delegate drone procurement authority down to commanders.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Since its establishment in January 2023, Neros progressed through venture backing and major U.S. Army contracts to secure substantial federal financing for domestic component manufacturing, signaling a broader U.S. defense shift toward onshored drone supply chains.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: U.S. Congress: export ban on Department of Defense procurement of uncrewed aircraft systems containing electronic components or critical subsystems from foreign countries of concern, including China (in_force).
U.S. Government: tariff on Imported drone components and consumer electronics (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Neros is scaling in-house manufacturing to meet domestic sourcing requirements and NDAA-compliant mandates.

items.title: U.S. National Defense Strategy Pushes to Supercharge Defense Industrial Base
items.summary: The U.S. National Defense Strategy officially called for national mobilization and supercharging the defense industrial base to scale weapons and ammunition production.

sections.label: What happened
lines: The U.S. National Defense Strategy officially called for national mobilization and supercharging the defense industrial base to scale weapons and ammunition production.

sections.label: Context
lines: 11 Jan 2024: The U.S. Department of Defense officially published the 2024 National Defense Industrial Strategy (NDIS) to build long-term industrial resilience.
15 Jan 2025: Pine Bluff Arsenal launched the ARSENAL READY campaign to modernize its industrial park infrastructure through public-private partnerships.
30 Oct 2026: Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle initiated high-level meetings in Arkansas to review Pine Bluff Arsenal's sole-source manufacturing capabilities.
Nov 2026: U.S. Army formally publicized strategic priorities integrating commercial supply chain practices (Walmart) and academic research (University of Arkansas).
8 Nov 2026: U.S. National Defense Strategy calls for national mobilization and 'supercharging' the defense industrial base to scale weapons and ammunition production.

sections.label: Policy direction
lines: US — 2026 National Defense Strategy (2026-01-23): Four lines of effort: defend the homeland (including Golden Dome missile defence), deter China in the Indo-Pacific, more burden-sharing by allies, and supercharge the US defence industrial base.

US — PAC-3 MSE framework agreement under the Acquisition Transformation Strategy (2026-01-06): Seven-year framework agreements for proven munitions, giving industry long-term demand so it invests in capacity; PAC-3 MSE output to rise from about 600 to about 2,000 a year, subject to Congress.

sections.label: The bigger picture
lines: Starting with the 2024 National Defense Industrial Strategy, policy has evolved toward long-term industrial resilience, culminating in the 2026 strategy's call to supercharge production and lower trade barriers Signal: expanded reliance on allied manufacturing.

sections.label: Down the supply chain
lines: Silicon Carbide Substrates depends on University of Arkansas Multi-User Silicon Carbide Research and Fabrication Facility.
U.S. Government: export licensing on chemical munitions and advanced semiconductor materials development (in_force).

US / International: sanction on International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR) controlling defense-related technical data, components, and dual-use manufacturing equipment, subject to proposed transatlantic trade barrier reductions outlined in the 2026 National Defense Strategy. (in_force).

sections.label: Why it matters
lines: Defense industry business development and procurement professionals should monitor changing transatlantic trade barriers and increased demand signals to align supply chains accordingly.

items.summary: Onodrim Industries raised $300 million in a Series A funding round led by Lux Capital, bringing its valuation to $1.3 billion. The company aims to acquire controlling stakes in businesses across critical European defence supply chains to alleviate manufacturing bottlenecks.

lines: Onodrim Industries raised $300 million in a Series A funding round led by Lux Capital, bringing its valuation to $1.3 billion. The company aims to acquire controlling stakes in businesses across critical European defence supply chains to alleviate manufacturing bottlenecks.

lines: 15 Dec 2015: Krauss-Maffei Wegmann (KMW) and Nexter Systems complete their formal merger to create the joint holding company KNDS (KMW + Nexter Defense Systems), headquartered in Amsterdam, structured as a 50/50 arrangement between the French state and the German founding families.
19 Feb 2025: KNDS hires financial advisers to explore a potential initial public offering (IPO) on public markets as early as late 2025 or 2026.
15 Sep 2025: KNDS management is instructed by the board to prepare for a public stock market listing, while discussions continue regarding a potential anchoring stake by the German government.

24 Jun 2026: The Bundestag's Budget Committee approves an initial ceiling of up to €7.2 billion for the federal state (acting through KfW) to acquire a 40% stake in KNDS linked to the planned IPO (Approved, EUR 7.2 billion).
Jul 2026: The planned dual-listing (IPO) of KNDS in Paris and Frankfurt is formally suspended due to unfavorable market valuations and investor resistance against valuation targets of ~€15 billion.
14 Oct 2026: Negotiations pivot toward a direct state purchase of the entire 50% German family-owned stake after institutional investors decline to meet valuation expectations.
5 Nov 2026: The German government and the Wegmann-Holding owner families reach a final agreement for the federal state to take over the 50% private stake directly (Agreement).

lines: 18 Mar 2019: BAE Systems announced an initial funding award from Lockheed Martin to commence integration work for MBDA's Meteor and SPEAR missiles onto the UK F-35 fleet.
